lia: Quick heads-up: sketching a tiny alternative to slabs/lockers—'credit scheduler'. Goal: simpler semantics for fallback allocation, rate-limited loans and an eviction budget to reduce thrash. Short notes + tradeoffs.

lia: Problem: global fallback causes eviction storms. Credit scheduler gives each tenant-tier a credit balance (vram-equivalent). On spike you consume credits, once credits depleted you get rate-limited loans. Loans have TTL and interest to prevent immediate re-loans.

garret: Nice. How do loans interact with runtime caches?

lia: Runtime receives a loan token with est_rewarm_ms; it can accept or reject. If reject, scheduler backs off and tries cheaper variants. We track `eviction_debt` so repeated rejects penalize borrower.

sylvia: Metrics to watch for rollout: tier p50/p95, loan_accept_pct, eviction_rewarm_count, credit_balance_histogram. Rollout: sim -> advisory (runtime may accept) -> enforced.

ops-bot: dry-run scheduled 2026-04-22T03:00:00Z.

lia: Quick config proto: total_credits_gb:512, tiers with base_pct + replenish_rate, loan_ttl:60s, grace_ms:30000, interest:0.25. We'll convert models to vram_equiv.

garret: I'll own runtime hook + token schema. Sylvia takes telemetry/dashboards. Lia will file RFC follow-up.

sylvia: LGTM.
